title: Pelvic floor muscle training
what: A specialist teaches you to find and strengthen the muscles at the bottom of the pelvis. They support the bladder, womb, and bowel.
why: After childbirth, for urine leaks when coughing or laughing, pelvic organ prolapse, after surgery, and during menopause.
duration: a session usually takes 30 to 60 minutes; a course usually lasts several weeks, with results after 2 to 3 months of regular practice
tell_doctor: If urine leaks, when, and how much
A heavy feeling or something bulging down below

prepare.title: Notes
prepare.text: For 2 to 3 days, write down how often you go to the toilet and when urine leaks.

prepare.title: Toilet
prepare.text: Go to the toilet before the session.

bring: Your referral, if you have one
steps: The specialist asks about the problem
Sometimes an exam is done to check muscle strength
They explain where these muscles are and how to find them
You learn to squeeze and relax them correctly, without tensing your belly or buttocks
Sometimes a device shows on a screen how your muscles are working
You get an exercise plan for home
feel: At first, it is hard to feel the right muscles. That is normal
after: Do the exercises every day as shown
Results usually show after 2 to 3 months
Come back for follow-up sessions to check progress

faq.q: Can I do the exercises on my own without a specialist?
faq.a: You can, but many people do them wrong. One or two sessions with a specialist help you do them right.

faq.q: Will exercises help with urine leaks?
faq.a: Often yes, especially with leaks when coughing or laughing. Regular practice is key.

faq.q: Can I start right after giving birth?
faq.a: Gentle exercises can usually start early. Your doctor will say when.

reminders.text: Pelvic floor session tomorrow. Bring comfortable clothes and your toilet notes.
